validity_findings.finding: Correctness oracle computed locally via generate_*_body(state, target_size) using same function as mock origin, rather than independent origin fetch without proxy. Oracle is valid because function is deterministic pure (json.dumps + padding, HTML/XML padded concatenation) and brotli.compress quality 6 is pure; IDENTITY baseline (120/120 at 1.0 across 3 content types) independently validates that local generation equals uncompressed server output. Independent fetch would be stronger but current method suffices within frozen design. No leakage or circularity beyond shared deterministic code.

claim_ceiling: Iterative decompression (brotli.decompress with gzip fallback, max_depth=5) produces byte-identical output to ground-truth deterministic generate_*_body(state, target_size) for all 4 auth states across 3 content types (JSON/HTML/XML) at 1KB nominal (compressed 70-176 bytes spanning 3-6 chunks at 32 bytes) for both MULTI-CHUNK (chunk_size=32) and SINGLE-CHUNK (chunk_size=1024) plus IDENTITY baseline, on localhost buffered Python Reverse Proxy -> Mock OAuth2 Flask-like server with brotli quality 6, N=10 per state per cell (360 total), seed 44, jitter 50-150ms, Python 3.12.14 brotli 1.2.0. Does NOT establish correctness on real CDN (Cloudflare/Fastly/Akamai), larger payloads (10KB/100KB), gzip multi-chunk, brotli quality variation (4-8), streaming partial-frame forwarding, production OAuth/OIDC middleware, or binary content. V1/V2 degeneracy from parent is resolved within this bounded setting; C-MEAS-VALID decompression-correctness blocker removed for this scope only, CDN testing remains required next gate.
